title: Indian Markets Surge as Iran Peace Deal Sends Oil Below $84 and Revives Inflow Hopes.
excerpt: Nifty jumps 1.5 per cent, rupee heads for 94.80, and BlackRock says India's $30 billion selloff was overdone. Here is what NRIs should know.
body:
Indian equities opened sharply higher on Monday morning, joining a global rally triggered by the U.S.-Iran peace deal that has sent oil prices tumbling and revived hopes that the worst of the foreign capital exodus may be over.

The benchmark Nifty 50 rose 1.53 per cent to 23,984.85 at the opening bell, while the BSE Sensex climbed 1.59 per cent to 76,725.27. All 16 major sectors advanced. Broader small-cap and mid-cap indices gained 1.6 per cent each. Oil marketing companies, tyre manufacturers, paint makers, and airlines — all heavy consumers of crude — led the charge.

The Indian rupee is expected to open in the 94.80–94.85 per dollar range, up from its Friday close of 95.11. If it holds, the currency will surpass the highs it reached after the Reserve Bank of India's June 5 policy announcement, which laid out a raft of measures to support the currency and attract dollar inflows.

## Oil Below $84: What It Means for India

Brent crude dived 4.5 per cent to $83.40 a barrel on Monday morning — its lowest level in more than three months — after U.S. President Donald Trump and Iran's deputy foreign minister confirmed a framework agreement to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

For India, the world's third-largest oil importer, cheaper crude is the single most powerful macro tailwind available. Lower oil prices ease pressure on inflation, narrow the trade deficit, and reduce the government's subsidy bill — a triple benefit that had been missing for the entire duration of the four-month U.S.-Iran conflict.

The war's toll on Indian markets has been severe. Foreign investors have pulled out a record $30 billion from Indian equities so far in 2026, fleeing to semiconductor-heavy markets like South Korea and Taiwan. The Nifty 50 and Sensex are still down roughly 11 per cent and 13 per cent, respectively, for the year.

## BlackRock Says India Has Been 'Over-Punished'

The rally comes days after BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager with over $14 trillion under management, said India's market had been "over-punished" for lacking a direct AI play and for its oil vulnerability. Natasha Sarkaria, EMEA investment strategy lead at BlackRock, said India remained one of the firm's "highest-conviction, medium- to long-term emerging-market trades," supported by demographics, infrastructure spending, and indirect AI-linked opportunities in power, data centres, and electrical equipment.

Lighthouse Canton echoed the view on Friday, arguing that India's lack of direct AI exposure could prove to be an "advantage of absence." Chief Investment Officer Abhay Laijawala said investors had "fatally underpriced" the concentration risk in South Korea and Taiwan, and that India offered a deep listed universe tied to the next phase of AI infrastructure spending.

## Bonds and the RBI Factor

The yield on India's 10-year benchmark bond ended at 6.8957 per cent on Friday, down 7 basis points for the week and posting its third consecutive weekly decline. Traders expect the yield to move in a 6.85–6.95 per cent range this week, with oil price movements and the U.S. Federal Reserve's first policy decision under Chair Kevin Warsh likely to set the direction.

Foreign investors have stepped up bond purchases sharply, buying a net 155.5 billion rupees in the six sessions since June 5 — overtaking the total for the entire year until that point. The RBI's measures, which include reviving a 2013-type window to mobilise funds from non-resident Indians, have been credited with building momentum behind the bond market rally.

## The NRI Angle

For NRIs, the market shift has immediate implications. The RBI's new FCNR deposit window offers decade-high dollar deposit rates at Indian banks — a move explicitly designed to attract diaspora capital. If crude remains anchored near $80 and portfolio flows return, the rupee's trajectory could make NRI remittances and property investments significantly cheaper in dollar terms.

The critical question, as one currency trader told Reuters, is the durability of the peace deal and, by extension, the sustainability of the drop in oil prices. The memorandum of understanding is scheduled to be signed on Friday in Switzerland. Until then, the rally has a tentative quality — but the direction, for now, is clear.
